title: What's in and out for creators heading into Q4
tldr: Digiday maps the creator economy shifts for Q4 2026: clipping, creators moving into the C-suite, diversification and looming regulation. A useful pulse-check on where creator work is heading.
why_fresh: forward-looking trend roundup on creator economy
angle: Write about 'creators in the C-suite' as the next phase of employee-generated and executive content.

title: How KitKat got teens to take a 'scroll break' on YouTube – with an 86% action rate
tldr: A campaign breakdown of KitKat's YouTube 'scroll break' targeting teens, hitting an 86% action rate. Concrete case study on aligning brand purpose (a break) with media-consumption behaviour.
why_fresh: concrete campaign case study with metrics
angle: Break down why a brand telling people to stop scrolling outperforms attention-grabbing tactics.

title: Mark Ritson: Digital marketing's endgame was always automation. Strategy matters again
tldr: Ritson argues that as AI automates execution, strategic thinking becomes the differentiator again. A contrarian take on where human value sits in an automated marketing stack.
angle: Argue that when everyone automates content, strategy and human judgment become the scarce asset.

title: How Facebook's News Feed introduced the age of the algorithm 20 years ago
tldr: A 20-year retrospective on the News Feed and how algorithmic curation reshaped how we consume media. Useful long-view context on media-consumption habits.
angle: Trace how 20 years of algorithmic feeds trained our content-consumption habits — and what comes after.

title: Music consumption trends 2026: Who's listening more – and what's driving discovery?
tldr: YouGov data on who is listening to more music in 2026 and what drives discovery. Direct read on how people consume audio content and where discovery happens.
angle: Use music discovery patterns as a proxy for how audiences find all content in 2026.

title: 5 toxic management behaviors that make good employees stop caring
tldr: Fast Company details management behaviours that erode engagement, arguing leaders often blame staff for conditions they created. Relevant to internal comms and employee engagement.
angle: Connect disengaged employees to the collapse of employee-generated content and internal advocacy.

title: AI Visibility is a PESO Model Problem—and You're Closer Than You Think
tldr: Gini Dietrich reframes the AI-visibility scramble as fundamentally a PESO (paid/earned/shared/owned) discipline, not a new tool problem. A grounding take amid AEO hype.
why_fresh: reframes AI visibility via established model
angle: Argue that 'AI visibility' is just integrated PESO with new distribution surfaces.

title: AEO mentions vs. citations: Key differences explained
tldr: HubSpot explains why brands show up in AI answers (mentions) without earning traffic (citations), and why measuring the wrong one distorts your picture. Practical for AI-era measurement.
angle: Explain the mention-vs-citation gap as the new attribution headache for content teams.

title: The Great Convergence: Everyone Sounds the Same. Now They're Becoming the Same Company.
tldr: State of Brand argues brand voices have homogenised to the point of convergence — with implications for differentiation in an AI-flattened content landscape.
angle: Make the case for human-centric, idiosyncratic content as the antidote to AI sameness.

title: Trust in AI starts with human-AI boundaries
tldr: Adobe's 2026 report finds consumers welcome AI in brand experiences but resist it becoming the primary interaction — only 19% want AI agents as their main touchpoint. A data-backed case for human-in-the-loop.
angle: Use the 19% stat to argue where humans must stay visible in AI-mediated brand content.

title: Newsroom AI and iD\TBWA Transform the New Audi Q3 into a Unique Brand Stories Experience
tldr: A campaign breakdown of how Audi turned a car launch into an AI-powered brand-storytelling ecosystem. Concrete example of modular, dynamic branded content at scale.
angle: Dissect how AI enables modular brand storytelling for product launches.

title: Compliance-First Content Architecture
tldr: Contently lays out a five-component workflow for regulated finance brands to scale content without breaking governance. Practical content architecture for high-stakes environments.
why_fresh: useful framework but not a new trend
angle: Show how governance-first architecture can be adapted beyond finance to any regulated comms.

title: Как рискнуть карьерой и не проиграть: Андрей Дороничев
tldr: Book excerpt on how YouTube walked away from 100M Apple users and saved itself — a strategic-decision narrative from an ex-Google exec. A story-driven look at high-stakes product/comms choices.
angle: Use YouTube's Apple gamble as a business-storytelling case on strategic sacrifice.

title: Как бизнесу интегрироваться в арт-ярмарки
tldr: SETTERS breaks down brand integrations at Cosmoscow art fair — artwashing risks, architect collabs and trends, with real examples from RBC to MR Group. A concrete look at experiential brand-culture partnerships.
angle: Explore when brand-art integration builds credibility vs slips into artwashing.

title: Crooked Media's nonprofit launches new political creator drive
tldr: Pod Save America's nonprofit arm is recruiting political creators to reach younger voters — a case of institutional media betting on distributed creator networks.
angle: Analyse orgs building owned creator armies instead of chasing earned reach.
